problem: Current RAG systems face challenges including independent chunk retrieval without considering relationships (redundancy and ordering), non-monotonic chunk utility where adding more chunks can degrade quality, and retrieval strategies failing to adapt to the unique characteristics of different queries (p.1-2).
methodology: The paper proposes CARROT, a cost-constrained retrieval optimization framework for RAG that adopts a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) based strategy using a cost-aware utility function and parallel evaluation to find the optimal chunk combination order (p.1, p.5-6). It also incorporates a configuration agent trained via contrastive learning to dynamically predict optimal rerankers and configurations for each query domain (p.1, p.4).
results: Experimental results demonstrate up to a 30% performance improvement over baseline methods, validating the framework's effectiveness, efficiency, and scalability (p.1, p.2).
key_findings: The Optimal Chunk Combination Order Selection problem is proven to be NP-hard (p.3). CARROT effectively addresses inter-chunk correlations, non-monotonic utility, and query intent diversity while minimizing token costs through budget constraints (p.2, p.4).
title: CARROT: A Learned Cost-Constrained Retrieval Optimization System for RAG
